semantic_boundary: own role-local clean state + public sources only; O, other-worker, downstream, legacy semantics excluded

finding.title: Pre-handle ambiguity has three distinct protocol families

families.name: server_minted_handle_after_create
families.reason: task may be durably created before CreateTaskResult reaches the requester; modern Tasks has no list operation to rediscover an unknown task id, so blind retry can duplicate task/effect unless application-level idempotency closes the gap

families.name: client_minted_stable_identity_before_create
families.reason: a deterministic client-chosen name can be retried as create-or-verify: on response loss/AlreadyExists, GET exact name and verify stable ownership/intent before adoption; UID distinguishes historical replacement and resourceVersion supplies later optimistic concurrency

families.name: server_minted_preflight_continuation_before_effect
families.example: MCP MRTR requestState used as a custom preflight fence
families.reason: first round must perform no effect and return integrity-bound requestState; requester durably persists it; second round uses a custom durable atomic create-or-get keyed by a stable operation identity inside/bound to requestState; retries verify and return the existing task/effect

evidence: JSON-RPC request id is a correlation identity, not a durable logical idempotency key; MRTR retries explicitly use a different JSON-RPC request id.
requestState is server-issued opaque continuation state returned with input_required; clients echo exact request params plus requestState on retry.
SEP-1050 recommends integrity protection and binding requestState to originating method, arguments, and principal/identity.
requestState only helps after it has reached and been persisted by the requester; direct Task creation still has a first-response-loss window.

A protocol-compliant preflight can move the stable continuation boundary before effects, but duplicate-safe creation still requires an atomic keyed create-or-get store/effect ledger; stock C# Tasks CreateTaskAsync interface previously pinned in own state has no such key.
C# server filters run before Tasks processing, which makes a custom pre-Tasks preflight/idempotency layer structurally plausible, not automatically provided.
mcp_current_protocol.negative: Never treat JSON-RPC request id itself as a durable idempotency key. Never treat requestState as closing a response-loss window that occurs before requestState was received.

safe_recipe: Choose deterministic metadata.name before mutation and include stable ownership/intent annotation or canonical intent hash.
On success, persist returned UID and resourceVersion.
On lost response or AlreadyExists, GET exact same name and verify apiVersion/kind plus stable ownership/intent and relevant spec identity; adopt only on exact match.
On mismatch, fail closed as name collision.
Use resourceVersion for subsequent read-modify-write CAS; after delete/recreate, reject stale identity because UID changes.
kubernetes_benchmark.counterexample: generateName is server-generated and does not give the caller a pre-known stable logical create identity; blind retry may create another object.

temporal_benchmark.finding: A stable client-chosen Workflow ID plus WorkflowIdConflictPolicy USE_EXISTING is a response-loss-recoverable start pattern for the workflow identity, but Temporal depends on persistent server/workers and therefore remains an external-executor benchmark rather than a direct Chat-native store mutation.

openhands_recovery_design.prior_source_level_gap: ordinary durable user MessageEvent may exist while persisted non-null active leaf and last_user_message_id remain old; cold load trusts non-null persisted leaf and existing startup repair is specific to unmatched executable ActionEvent

unique_descendant_reconcile.safe_subset: advance only across exactly one structurally valid descendant chain and fail closed on forks
unique_descendant_reconcile.remaining_problem: unique graph structure does not itself prove that the descendant was intended to become the active branch in a system supporting retrospective forks

fenced_commit_marker.classification: FENCED_COMMIT_RECOVERABLE within supported local-filesystem durability scope
write_protocol: While holding ConversationLease generation G and expected old leaf L, durably write pending marker containing G, L, new event id E, parent/hash, and head-derived updates.
Persist event E with parent L and exact-readback/hash it.
Persist base_state active leaf E and derived last_user_message_id.
Clear marker only after exact verification.
restart_protocol: If marker exists and head is L, E exists with exact expected parent/hash and no conflicting marker/fork, a takeover writer may finish the prior fenced intent then clear marker.
If head already equals E and E verifies, clear stale marker.
If E is missing, do not advance head; marker can be abandoned/cleared according to recovery policy.
If head moved to an incompatible F, multiple markers exist, or event/hash/parent conflicts, fail closed instead of tail-picking.
fenced_commit_marker.scope_limit: Do not generalize the local file lease/ordering argument to NFS/network filesystems where the pinned source already warns flock is unreliable. Preserve the existing unmatched executable Action repair as a separate recovery class.

control25_revision_note: Previous control24 zero-residual-executor oracle is stale for positive acceptance. Under control25, exhaust all safely Chat-capable work first; a remaining protected/primary-writer capability may be recorded only as a generic downstream-verification-required boundary, never as CLEAN-final acceptance.

generic_residual_boundary.status: none asserted for this research leaf
generic_residual_boundary.reason: The current work is public/source analysis plus role-local artifact/checkpoint mutation, all of which was Chat-capable. Future implementation against an external protected system must be capability-audited rather than assumed unavailable.

acceptance_counterexamples: Lost direct MCP CreateTaskResult plus no task id => unknown created task; blind retry unsafe.
JSON-RPC request id reused as logical operation key => blocked: correlation semantics do not establish durable idempotency.
MCP requestState received but custom store lacks atomic create-or-get => partial only.
MRTR preflight creates effect before client persists requestState => does not close first-response-loss.
Kubernetes deterministic name exists but intent/ownership mismatch => collision, fail closed.
Kubernetes same name after delete/recreate but UID differs => historical identity changed; reject stale adoption.
Kubernetes generateName response lost => caller lacks stable pre-known name; blind retry can duplicate.
OpenHands unique descendant under fork-capable history => structure alone insufficient to prove active intent.
OpenHands marker valid + event valid + stale head => recoverable completion candidate.
OpenHands marker/head/event conflict => BLOCKED; never choose log tail by recency.
frontier: Prototype the MCP MRTR preflight create-or-get pattern against current protocol/source: determine the smallest custom server/filter/store surface that can durably bind requestState operation identity before built-in Tasks creation without inventing unsupported protocol semantics.

Turn the OpenHands fenced commit-marker matrix into an exact v1.44.1 patch/regression candidate while preserving unmatched Action repair and intentional fork semantics; keep source-level only if dependencies remain unavailable.
Find another open-source mutating API with a caller-supplied idempotency identity plus exact lookup/readback after response loss, preferably a surface plausibly exposed to Chat connectors.

Audit actually connected mutation surfaces for Kubernetes-like deterministic create + exact GET + CAS patterns and distinguish Chat-capable predecessors from any genuinely protected residual effect under control25.
termination: Frontier persisted; semantic exploration stops at current invocation runtime boundary, not completion.
